acceptance_checks: verify_pure_base_sync performs no network or API call, and every git invocation is read-only and runs with cwd=target.
No git invocation in the module has its failure swallowed (no `|| true`, no bare except that continues).
A single clean sync, two consecutive clean syncs, and a base that did not move each prove.
An evil merge is refused by the tree-reproduction step while the first-parent, no-authored-commit and arity steps all PASS — asserted explicitly.
`git merge -s ours <base>` is refused by the tree-reproduction step with the earlier steps passing.
A .gitattributes merge=union is refused before the tree-reproduction step runs.
An octopus merge, an authored non-merge commit, a reversed merge direction, and a second parent that is not an ancestor of the base are each refused by their own step.
A superseded feature tip passes the arity/ancestry step and is refused by tree reproduction.
A commit-tree-forged merge with correct parents and an arbitrary tree is refused.
An orphaned a_sha is refused, with an assertion that no network call was attempted.
A shallow repository is refused with a distinct shallow reason.
An unavailable or failing merge-tree capability probe refuses the carry.
Every test builds a real temporary git repository; git is never mocked.
The module is registered in shiki_installer.py TEMPLATE_PATHS and in test_shiki_module_boundaries.sh.
No file outside the declared locks is changed.
non_goals: Any network or GitHub API lookup
Persisting the proof to a file
Tolerating a merge that required conflict resolution
Reading or writing any approval state
Touching any file outside the declared locks

findings.detail: _tree_has_gitattributes runs `git ls-tree -r --name-only` and matches `Path(line).name == ".gitattributes"`. Without `-z`, git C-quotes paths containing newlines/control chars (e.g. a directory named with an embedded newline), so a real in-tree `.gitattributes` at such a path would render as a quoted string whose Path().name is not exactly ".gitattributes" and would be MISSED. Since `git merge-tree` honors in-tree `.gitattributes` merge drivers regardless of `core.attributesFile=/dev/null` (that setting only overrides the global attributes file, not in-tree ones), step 3 is the real defense against an in-tree `merge=union` driver — and this gap lets a contrived directory name slip one past it. Impact is bounded (only built-in drivers like union are reachable from in-tree attributes since custom drivers require .git/config the attacker can't set on the runner; union merely concatenates reviewed-A and trusted-base content) and requires attacker control of a special-char directory path plus a base edit under it, and the module is a not-yet-wired primitive — so this is a hardening note, not blocking. Suggest `git ls-tree -r -z --name-only` split on NUL, or scanning for the basename in the raw entries.
findings.title: step 3 .gitattributes detection can be evaded by special-character paths (ls-tree without -z)

scope:
Add `scripts/shiki_sync_proof.py` exposing `verify_pure_base_sync(*, target, a_sha, head_sha, default_branch) -> SyncProof`, where `SyncProof` carries `proved: bool`, `reason: str` and the merge count. It is the ONLY module in the guardian family that runs git; every git invocation is read-only, runs with `cwd=target`, and no invocation may be suffixed with `|| true` or have its failure swallowed.

Conditions, in this order, each failure recorded as a distinct reason:
  1. `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` is false; `refs/remotes/origin/<default_branch>^{commit}` resolves; `git rev-parse HEAD` equals `head_sha`. A shallow repository is reported distinctly so the caller can fail the step loudly rather than silently not carrying.
  2. Capability probe: `git merge-tree --write-tree <head> <head>` exits 0 and prints 40 hex characters. (Requires git >= 2.38; the probe is what makes an older runner fail closed rather than mysteriously.)
  3. No path named `.gitattributes` exists in the trees of `a_sha`, `head_sha` or the base, and every merge-tree invocation passes `-c core.attributesFile=/dev/null`. A `merge=union` attribute can reprogram what a merge produces, which would let a merge be simultaneously 'mechanical' and attacker-chosen.
  4. `a_sha` resolves as a LOCAL object (`git cat-file -e`). Never fall back to any network or API lookup: an API lookup serves commits orphaned by a force-push, which is exactly the case this condition exists to reject.
  5. `a_sha != head_sha` (equal needs no carry).
  6. `a_sha` appears in `git rev-list --first-parent <head_sha>`.
  7. `git rev-list --first-parent --no-merges <a_sha>..<head_sha>` is empty.
  8. Every commit in `git rev-list --first-parent <a_sha>..<head_sha>` has EXACTLY two parents and its second parent is an ancestor of the base.
  9. THE PROOF: `git -c core.attributesFile=/dev/null merge-tree --write-tree <a_sha> <base>` exits 0 (no conflict) and its output equals `git rev-parse <head_sha>^{tree}`.
Any exception is caught at the function boundary and returns `proved=False` with the exception named. There is no branch that returns `proved=True` without step 9 having run and matched.

Register the module in `scripts/shiki_installer.py` TEMPLATE_PATHS and in `scripts/test_shiki_module_boundaries.sh`.

Add `tests/test_sync_proof.py` building REAL temporary git repositories — no mocks of git — one per case: a single clean sync proves; two consecutive clean syncs prove; a base that did not move proves; an evil merge (hand-edited merge tree) with a payload in a base-touched path is refused by step 9 while steps 6-8 pass, asserted explicitly so step 9 is proved load-bearing; `git merge -s ours <base>` is refused by step 9 with steps 6-8 passing; a `.gitattributes` with `merge=union` is refused by step 3 BEFORE step 9 runs; an octopus merge is refused by the arity check; an authored non-merge commit after `a_sha` is refused by step 7; a reversed merge (base merged the feature) is refused by step 6; a merge whose second parent is not an ancestor of the base is refused by step 8; a superseded feature tip merged in — reachable from base but stale — passes step 8 and is refused by step 9; a `commit-tree`-forged merge with an arbitrary tree and correct parents is refused by step 9; an orphaned `a_sha` is refused by step 4 with an assertion that no network call was attempted; a shallow clone is refused with the distinct shallow reason.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task builds, and what to change to get the same result.
  Problem: branch protection has `required_status_checks.strict = true`, so a PR that goes BEHIND must merge its base in before it can merge; that changes the head SHA; and `guardian_comment.require_head_sha` is true, so the approval already granted for the reviewed content is discarded. Measured on 2026-08-01: landing five Contract PRs cost four extra operator approvals, one per PR per merge round, with no content change whatsoever between them.
  Why tree reproduction and not a diff: measured in throwaway repositories — `git merge -s ours <base>` yields an identical `git diff A H` while reverting the base entirely, and an evil merge can carry a payload while touching zero paths outside those the base itself touched. Both defeat every cheaper check. Step 9 is the criterion; steps 6-8 are pre-rejects and bound which `a_sha` may be named.
  Measured yield, so the rule is known to fire: on the real PR #237 sync (A=7f34529a72a14c076adae67bee1cd8a390ce8df0, H=fa826dbe0b5a5670cf0aa5994f042e7592ff41d2, base=3bdda917d6e1f3e879a55f6eb7c7478640e8d896) with git 2.54.0, step 6 PASS, step 7 count 0, step 8 arity 2 with the second parent an ancestor of base, and step 9 produced a0566fcca76b075a48693e461921efe616ea1408 which equals tree(H) exactly. A synthetic two-sync history with disjoint paths also proved. A sync where both sides edited the same file conflicts, so the carry is refused and the operator resolves it — the correct outcome.
  Known landmine: `git merge-tree --write-tree` needs git >= 2.38 and the runner's version is NOT verified by this repository. That is why the capability probe is a condition rather than an assumption: an older runner must refuse the carry loudly, never silently mis-prove one.
  Reproducible when: every attack case above is refused with the step that refused it named, and the real #237 shape proves.
test_command: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests && bash scripts/test_shiki_module_boundaries.sh && python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target .
title: Prove from git that a push was a pure base-sync
